players.product: foundation IP (SRAM compilers, standard cells) and high-speed interface IP

quarterly_data.signal: 1Q26 results (company deck): net revenue NT$394,748 thousand (US$12,467 thousand), down 27.5% QoQ and 9.2% YoY; gross margin 100%; operating margin -16.8%; net loss NT$49,247 thousand; EPS NT$-1.18. Company: the decline was mainly due to delayed U.S. fabless customer projects and fewer working days during the Lunar New Year; operating expenses rose ~8% YoY, driven by higher R&D investment to support business scaling and advanced process development.
quarterly_data.figure: 1Q26 revenue NT$394,748 thousand (-27.5% QoQ, -9.2% YoY); EPS NT$-1.18

quarterly_data.signal: 1Q26 revenue mix (company deck): license fees 81.9% and royalties 18.1% of revenue (the royalty share rebounded, a nearly 20% QoQ increase); China and Taiwan together 88.6% of revenue, while the USA share fell below 10% due to project delays; foundry customers 52.5% of revenue (31.9% in 2024), a roughly 50:50 fabless / foundry split. 16nm-and-below nodes contributed 57.9% of license revenue, driven by sub-8nm foundry projects and AI / automotive demand from China fabless customers; new 2-8nm foundry platform engagements lifted 2-8nm to 79% of foundry license fees. Sub-16nm royalty revenue increased by nearly 700% YoY, while royalty revenue from mature nodes at 22nm and above declined by approximately 20% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: license 81.9% / royalty 18.1%; 16nm-and-below 57.9% of license revenue; sub-16nm royalty revenue up nearly 700% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Company outlook: looking ahead to 2026, M31 expects advanced-node project demand from U.S. customers to gain momentum, while strong demand from China in high-end imaging, ADAS, IoT wireless connectivity chips and tablet processors is expected to support overall revenue performance; it expects more meaningful advanced-node royalty contributions in 2026 as customers ramp mass production.

Interface IP updates (company deck): TSMC N2P (2nm) eUSB2V2 tapeout, deeply co-optimized with TSMC for AI, HPC and mobile SoCs; 4nm M-PHY v5.0 silicon-proven and advancing to 3nm, reaching 23.32Gbps (HS-G5) per lane and integrating with UFSHCI v4.1 and UniPro IP for a complete UFS 4.1 solution for mobile, automotive and AI edge devices.
quarterly_data.figure: TSMC N2P eUSB2V2 tapeout; 4nm M-PHY v5.0 at 23.32Gbps per lane

quarterly_data.signal: Customers and licences (company deck): 477 customers till 1Q26 (455 fabless, 22 foundry), incl. 267 in China, 77 in the USA and 80 in Taiwan; 73 new licences in 1Q26 (199 in 2025), 1918 cumulative. 2025 revenue US$57.3M, up 24.4% YoY. Monthly revenue: April 2026 NT$168,686K, up 30.74% YoY; 2026 accumulated revenue NT$563,434K, -0.02% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: 477 customers; 73 new licences in 1Q26; April 2026 revenue NT$168,686K (+30.74% YoY)
